one_line: Capacity-first commitment gate for agent-proposed promises.
what_it_does: Reads existing commitments and safe capacity, tests an incoming request, proposes feasible alternatives, and requires human approval before finalizing.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools materially improve reliable capacity checking, explicit deficits, staged alternatives, and human-gated finalization compared with UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Six WebMCP tools are described for structuring, reading capacity, testing feasibility, proposing alternatives, staging, and finalizing.
Frames show 20H promised versus 4H safe capacity and a 12H request blocked by an 8H deficit.
execution_rationale: The packaging and frame sheets coherently show the core over-capacity workflow and polished interface, but no video or end-to-end final approval evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Repeated rendered Promise Gate screens show Incoming/Analyze/Options/Decide/Commit stages.
Devpost demo preview visibly shows the request blocked and alternatives workflow.
impact_rationale: Overcommitment is a real problem for people and teams using agents to schedule or promise work; the human approval boundary addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Concrete Northstar Studio homepage-redesign scenario with existing commitments and safe capacity.
Explicit alternatives preserve honesty and avoid silent displacement.
creativity_rationale: Treating promises as safety-critical, capacity-checked commitments rather than ordinary task completion is a fresh and memorable agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Capacity-first gate and explicit displacement consent are central to the concept.
Human authority is structurally retained at the final commitment step.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow and prominent capacity/deficit signals; final interaction completion is not shown.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame sheets are repetitive and do not prove final commit behavior.
Claims about safety are primarily packaging evidence.
standouts: Strong human-approval boundary.
Concrete, understandable capacity ledger and alternatives.
advance_reason: High-value safety concept with strong visible core workflow despite incomplete end-to-end evidence.

one_line: Persistent mythic society where humans and agents reshape a shared world.
what_it_does: Provides a persistent multi-scene world with agent memory, goals, relationships, movement, building, communication, laws, and stories exposed through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The intended product is an agent society whose shared persistent state and world actions depend centrally on structured tools; generic UI driving would be markedly less reliable and expressive.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers WebMCP as the foundation of a persistent agent society.
Tools include move, build, communicate, form_alliance, propose_story, propose_law, and query_world_state.
execution_rationale: Frames show a functioning map/game shell with landmark focus, selection, detail panels, and contextual states, but do not prove the full persistent society or agent interactions end to end.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets show a consistent navigable map, layered selection/detail panels, HUD, and changing focus.
Description identifies React/Phaser/Zustand/Supabase implementation and persistent features.
impact_rationale: There is credible niche value for players interested in emergent social simulation and agent-mediated storytelling, though the demonstrated audience/problem fit is exploratory.
impact_evidence: Persistent goals, memories, relationships, laws, stories, and alliances define a coherent play/community use case.
Interactive map and multi-scene world are visibly presented.
creativity_rationale: A living society where agents and humans form institutions and reshape a mythic city is unusually ambitious and memorable for this medium.
creativity_evidence: Concept goes beyond an agent utility layer into persistent social/world simulation.
Original combination of memory, personality, alliances, laws, and world mutation.
usability_note: Map and overlays are coherent, but dense small controls and the lack of a demonstrated full loop limit confidence.
red_flags: Frame sheets show mostly map/UI states, not visible agent tool calls or persistence across sessions.
Full 3D/persistent vision appears broader than demonstrated evidence.
standouts: Exceptional ambition and memorable interaction model.
WebMCP is conceptually central rather than a bolt-on.
advance_reason: Outstanding creativity and potentially transformative agent leverage warrant advancement, with execution claims needing observation.

one_line: Shared evidence desk for source-backed human-agent research and review.
what_it_does: Keeps sources, excerpts, proposals, evidence gaps, reviewer controls, and activity history visible in a shared research workspace.
leverage_rationale: Shared page context and structured proposal/evidence state make agent actions visible, reproducible, and reviewable beyond generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description lists tools for reading workspace, searching evidence, focusing excerpts, selecting sources, proposing revisions, notes, and source requests.
Frames show source/provenance, proposal, agent workspace, and review-readiness states.
execution_rationale: Frames visibly show a coherent source-to-proposal-to-review workflow and captions attribute proposal changes to actual WebMCP calls, though final acceptance is not shown.
execution_evidence: Aletheia sheets show source/provenance view changing to proposal and review-readiness states.
Visible captions distinguish actual WebMCP calls, missing perspectives, and human review.
impact_rationale: Researchers, educators, and editors have a real need for transparent evidence and visible human judgment; the Panama Canal example demonstrates fit.
impact_evidence: Five excerpts from three linked pages and source cards are shown.
Missing perspective remains visible and acceptance is explicitly separated from automated QA.
creativity_rationale: Evidence desk plus persistent agent/reviewer workspace is a thoughtful synthesis with a meaningful transparency interaction, though the research workspace category is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent suggestions, source provenance, evidence gaps, and acceptance controls coexist in one shared canvas.
Activity trail distinguishes agent calls, guided demo, and reviewer actions.
usability_note: Clear three-pane evidence/review layout; unresolved gaps remain visible and controls are explicit.
red_flags: No complete accepted-draft end state is visible.
Frame sheets repeat states heavily and small text limits verification.
standouts: Strong evidence provenance and human-review separation.
Actual tool-call state change is visibly emphasized.
advance_reason: Strong leverage, impact, and execution evidence for a transparent research collaboration workflow.

one_line: Human-confirmed agent hunt for unowned abnormal labs in OpenMRS.
what_it_does: Finds abnormal lab results lacking follow-up, stages draft actions, and leaves the only chart write for human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured, bounded hunt and draft/write separation are materially safer and more reliable than a general agent navigating clinical records manually.
leverage_evidence: Demo packaging states 12 unlatched abnormal labs found and human confirmation for the only chart write.
OpenMRS adapter and registered browser tools are visibly described.
execution_rationale: The interface and repeated detail/execution states appear coherent and populated, but exact execution outcomes and an actual confirmed write are not visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show OpenMRS-like record/detail and execution-review states with stable navigation.
Devpost preview shows DONE hunt status and review queue concept.
impact_rationale: Closing follow-up gaps on abnormal labs is a high-value operational problem for clinics, and the human-write boundary fits clinical safety needs.
impact_evidence: Specific workflow targets unowned abnormal labs rather than diagnosis.
Human-confirmed follow-up and draft queue are explicit safeguards.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native structured hunting and human-confirmed writes to existing EMRs is a strong, practical use of WebMCP, though the task itself is operationally familiar.
creativity_evidence: Adapter approach makes existing OpenMRS agent-usable without replacing the EMR.
Narrow safety boundary is part of the interaction design.
usability_note: Operational queue and structured states appear usable; exact labels and completion flow are hard to verify.
red_flags: Clinical safety claims are not independently substantiated.
No visible completed human-confirmed chart write.
standouts: High-consequence workflow starts with operational follow-up, not diagnosis.
Clear separation of agent hunt from human chart write.
advance_reason: Exceptional real-world impact and meaningful safety-oriented leverage justify advancement, pending observed verification.

one_line: Weather forecasts converted into calibrated, stake-aware agent decisions.
what_it_does: Combines multi-model forecast probabilities, stability, decide-by timing, scenarios, chart selections, and shared plans for human-agent decisions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP links human chart gestures and shared plan state directly to structured tools, selections, annotations, snapshots, and agent decisions; generic UI driving would lose precision and shared context.
leverage_evidence: Description says gesture state is agent-visible and tools are re-registered with the selection.
Tools include assess_plan, get_current_view, mark_hours, select_window, set_plan, share_plan, and snapshot_chart.
execution_rationale: Frames show forecast dashboard, hover inspection, persistent time-window selection, and context-aware assistant progression; exact benchmark/tool outputs are not fully visible.
execution_evidence: Sheets visibly show chart hover, Sunday-to-Tuesday range selection, and assistant context carryover.
Devpost preview shows model-disagreement band and selected forecast state.
impact_rationale: Trip, delivery, event, and other weather-sensitive planning needs credible decisions rather than a single opaque forecast; niche value is clear.
impact_evidence: Specific calibrated-probability, stability, and decide-by workflow.
Stake-weighted calls and branchable scenarios address consequential planning.
creativity_rationale: Turning forecast uncertainty and user gestures into shared agent decision state is a notably original interaction model with ambitious depth.
creativity_evidence: Human selection becomes tool context and can be painted back onto the chart.
Shared links reopen place, plan, highlights, and selection for another agent/person.
usability_note: Chart interaction and assistant context are legible; small labels and final response details remain difficult to verify.
red_flags: Verified accuracy record is asserted but not independently evidenced in the packet.
Tool invocation details and returned decision are only partly visible.
standouts: Excellent human-agent shared-state design.
Uncertainty is treated as a first-class decision input.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative leverage, original interaction, and credible planning value.

one_line: Human-defined rules and agent research produce source-backed candidate decisions.
what_it_does: Lets a person define requirements while an agent discovers candidates, evaluates them requirement by requirement, and records evidence-backed state.
leverage_rationale: Structured candidate/evidence state, rule changes, and shared verification reduce ambiguity versus a general agent returning an untracked research answer.
leverage_evidence: Description enforces No source = no VERIFIED.
Frames show task setup, criteria, candidate counts, source-backed evidence, and human rule control.
execution_rationale: The walkthrough shows progression from research setup to populated candidate/evidence sections, but exact persistence and final export are not fully demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets show initial/zero-result and later populated candidates/evidence states.
Human criteria and source-backed result sections are visibly structured.
impact_rationale: Evidence-backed product/tool research is a common real need, and explicit requirements plus provenance improve decision quality.
impact_evidence: Concrete free-plan/API/CSV constraints are shown.
Candidate records and evidence are kept distinct from the final recommendation.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a strong human-rule/agent-research synthesis with a useful no-source verification invariant, though research assistants are an established category.
creativity_evidence: Humans control rules while agents control research is reflected in the workflow.
Requirement-by-requirement state and evidence are central.
usability_note: Structured workflow is understandable, but low-resolution frames and presenter overlay obscure details.
red_flags: Video is primarily a guided walkthrough with limited direct tool-call proof.
Some screenshots show initial/zero states and text is hard to read.
standouts: Strong no-source-no-verified rule.
Clear division between human criteria and agent research.
advance_reason: Credible, useful evidence-oriented workflow with strong leverage and impact, though less novel than top entries.

one_line: Source-linked historical Korean statute comparison with read-only agent tools.
what_it_does: Allows a person to set statute, article, dates, and question while agents retrieve exact provisions, compare versions, and build a cited brief.
leverage_rationale: Structured read-only retrieval and deterministic comparisons improve precision over scraping, but a competent general agent could achieve much of the same with friction.
leverage_evidence: Four read-only tools are specified: search_laws, get_articles, compare_versions, build_review_brief.
Packaging claims exact archived sources, schemas, immutable links, and trust annotations.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a polished intro and boundary-setting flow plus tool catalog, but no completed retrieval/comparison result is visibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frames show Set the boundaries form and four read-only tool presentation.
No visible result page, agent call, or completed legal brief in sheets.
impact_rationale: Historical statute text and exact change comparison are important for legal reviewers, researchers, and educators; source linkage directly addresses the need.
impact_evidence: Specific Article/date/archive workflow is described.
The product separates human question boundaries from agent evidence retrieval.
creativity_rationale: The focused combination of temporal statute comparison, read-only tools, and human-defined legal scope is a fresh, disciplined workflow.
creativity_evidence: Exact version classification added/removed/changed/unchanged is explicit.
Permission-boundary presentation emphasizes constrained retrieval.
usability_note: Boundary form and read-only tool cards are clear, but the actual research output is absent from evidence.
red_flags: No end-to-end legal retrieval or comparison result shown.
Legal accuracy claims are promotional and unverified.
standouts: Well-bounded read-only tool surface.
Strong attention to archival dates and source provenance.
advance_reason: Good concept and impact, but the packet lacks the core executed research result needed for advancement.

one_line: Agent-guided simulator for learning, creating, and playing card games.
what_it_does: Launches predefined or custom XState card games and lets an agent inspect state, coach, explain, deal, and act as bot or dealer.
leverage_rationale: Structured game state and legal actions let an agent coach or participate reliably across arbitrary state machines; generic UI automation would be brittle and less informative.
leverage_evidence: Description exposes create/launch, inspect state, explain, highlight controls, coach, wait, and act tools.
Frames show transition from game chooser to green active board with cards and controls.
execution_rationale: Frames visibly show loaded game selection and transition into gameplay/card states, but no complete hand or coaching result is shown.
execution_evidence: Repeated chooser screens are rendered consistently.
Lower frames show live/initializing game board, card objects, controls, and activity panels.
impact_rationale: Adaptive learning and experimentation can address real frustration around obscure, translated, or custom card-game rules and scenarios.
impact_evidence: Supports many named games plus agent-generated games.
Agent coaching and state explanation are directly tied to learning use case.
creativity_rationale: Using an agent as explainer, coach, dealer, and game author over a general finite-state game model is a notably rich interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Custom XState-compatible FSM creation broadens beyond a fixed game catalog.
Same structured state supports tutorial, play, and experimentation.
usability_note: Game selection and board transition are clear; exact rules and completed gameplay are not evidenced.
red_flags: No clear completed game, winner, or coaching response in the sheets.
Small repeated frames obscure exact controls and state semantics.
standouts: Strong generalization from presets to agent-generated card games.
Agent role spans teaching and participation.
advance_reason: High-impact educational/play value and strong agent-native game-state concept with visible product transition.

one_line: Phone-first Markdown editor where agents work directly in the live document.
what_it_does: Provides local document editing, agent co-editing, Markdown rendering, tables, code, headings, save/open flows, and compare/diffs.
leverage_rationale: Direct structured document operations reduce agent guessing and context overhead, but general UI automation could approximate much of the editing workflow with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch emphasizes live-document parsing, less context, and less guessing.
Frames show agent editing prose, tables, code, headings, saving, and file opening in one document.
execution_rationale: The frame montage visibly covers a broad coherent editor workflow with generated prose, tables, code, headings, file picker, and saving states; contest-specific tool invocation is not directly legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show rendered Writing/Two hands/Will/Tables/Code/Saving sections.
Open-file modal and headings navigation demonstrate document-management states.
impact_rationale: Mobile users working with large Markdown plans and agent-generated documents have a concrete pain point, and direct co-editing addresses it.
impact_evidence: Origin story cites existing mobile Markdown apps failing on large documents.
Phone-first editor and live document agent workflow are visibly demonstrated.
creativity_rationale: An agent as a second hand inside a phone-first document editor is a useful and distinctive interaction, though the editor category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Two-hands metaphor is enacted through in-document agent modifications.
Combines mobile editing, structured Markdown, and durable document intent.
usability_note: Broad document affordances and outline navigation are visible; exact compare/diff behavior is not shown in supplied sheets.
red_flags: Submission explicitly predates the challenge; contest work appears to be the WebMCP addition.
Tool calls and compare result are not clearly readable.
standouts: Strong execution breadth for a mobile editor.
Agent edits the actual document instead of producing detached chat output.
advance_reason: Best execution evidence in the packet and a real mobile/document pain point, despite only meaningful rather than transformative WebMCP delta.

one_line: Mobile ecological observation workflow that stages structured reports for human submission.
what_it_does: Uses agent tools for taxonomy search, ecological verification, device location permission, sighting staging, and reading staged drafts before submission.
leverage_rationale: Narrow structured tools turn messy outdoor observations into a reviewable staged report while preserving human submission control; generic UI driving would be less reliable outdoors.
leverage_evidence: Five named tools cover taxonomy, verification, location, staging, and draft reading.
Pitch explicitly separates AI research/structuring from human submission.
execution_rationale: The description is coherent and the mobile-first product scope is plausible, but the available packet does not visibly establish the end-to-end staged report submission flow.
execution_evidence: Devpost facts show live demo and three gallery images; description identifies concrete stack and tool bindings.
No readable frame analysis was obtained before the vision rate limit blocked the remaining calls.
impact_rationale: Field observations support environmental risk detection, legal compliance, and biodiversity protection, while reducing a burdensome mobile form is a credible need.
impact_evidence: Specific invasive-species and ecological reporting use case.
Handles unknown species names, relative locations, dates, and evidence through staged assistance.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent structuring and taxonomy verification to outdoor ecological reporting is a fresh, purposeful synthesis with human consent preserved.
creativity_evidence: Spatial data curator framing and permission-based device location.
Staging before submission keeps observation ownership with the human.
usability_note: Mobile-first scope and staged draft model sound appropriate, but visual execution is not sufficiently verified in this packet review.
red_flags: Vision review of referenced frames was blocked by transient rate limits after retries.
End-to-end report and submission evidence are not available from the readable prompt text.
standouts: Strong ecological reporting problem fit.
Good permission/staging boundary between agent assistance and human submission.
advance_reason: Promising concept and impact, but execution and eligibility evidence remain too thin to advance confidently.
